service_boundary: Represents Vercel's gateway service, not the upstream providers or Vercel's wider hosting platform.
regional_controls: No customer control over processing geography is documented for the gateway itself; upstream provider selection determines where processing occurs.
retention_controls: Zero-retention handling is documented both per request and as a chargeable team-wide setting, and customer-supplied provider keys are supported on paid plans.
routing: Requests can fall back across providers, and customer-supplied keys are used first with documented fallback to platform credentials when a key fails.
customization: The service routes existing hosted models; no customer fine-tuning or private model deployment is documented.
strengths: Documentation states plainly that no markup and no platform fee are applied to tokens, and dates itself, which is rare among comparable services.
Budgets can be scoped to a team, project, key, or member rather than only to an account.
Observability exports through open telemetry drains rather than a proprietary console only.
tradeoffs: A failed request using a customer-supplied key falls back to platform credentials and that usage is billed, so key failures carry a silent cost.
The free tier reaches a subset of the catalogue, and free credits stop applying permanently once credits are purchased.
Team-wide provider allowlisting and zero retention are billed per request, while their per-request equivalents are free.

response_integrity.note: No signature, attestation, or equivalent mechanism for verifying that a response arrived unaltered from the upstream model appears in the AI Gateway overview, the security and compliance pages, the zero-data-retention page, the FAQ, or the provider routing documentation.
response_integrity.scope: Vercel AI Gateway security and compliance documentation, for Vercel AI Gateway

upstream_disclosure.note: The privacy notice lists "AI providers in connection with providing you Vercel's AI Products and Services" among the parties data is disclosed to, and the AI Gateway zero-data-retention page names the upstream providers individually, from Alibaba Cloud and Anthropic through Together AI and xAI.
upstream_disclosure.scope: Vercel privacy notice, for Vercel AI Gateway

credential_handling.note: A platform-wide statement rather than an AI Gateway one: the security page states "Data is encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (HTTPS / TLS), including sensitive information like access tokens and secrets." The AI Gateway bring-your-own-key page describes team-scoped credentials and fallback to Vercel's own credentials but does not restate encryption at rest.
credential_handling.scope: Vercel security page, read for AI Gateway bring-your-own-key credentials

cache_isolation.note: The zero-data-retention page states: "When you use prompt caching through AI Gateway, caching happens at the provider level. Whether that caching is ZDR-compliant depends on the provider." Nothing states whether cache entries are scoped per team or pooled across customers reaching the same provider through Vercel's credentials.
cache_isolation.scope: Vercel AI Gateway zero-data-retention page, for Vercel AI Gateway

vulnerability_disclosure.note: A platform-wide security.txt names a disclosure programme ("Contact: https://hackerone.com/vercel-open-source") and a responsible-disclosure mailbox. AI Gateway is operated on the same domain under the same policy.
vulnerability_disclosure.scope: Vercel security.txt, for Vercel AI Gateway

independent_audit.note: The compliance page states "Vercel has a SOC 2 Type 2 attestation for Security, Confidentiality, and Availability" company-wide, and neither it, the SOC 2 FAQ, nor the public trust centre names AI Gateway or states that the attestation covers every product. Recorded as undocumented for the named service.
independent_audit.scope: Vercel compliance documentation, read for AI Gateway scope
